Colombia–Mexico Tax Treaty and Limited Liability Partnership Exchange of Information Protocol (in force 2013)
Pacific Alliance Framework Agreement with Chile, Mexico, and Peru (investment and services liberalization)
Andean Community Decision 578 for sub-regional investment and double taxation avoidance

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 526 de 1999 (UIAF), Ley 1121 de 2006 (PEP & anti-laundering), Decreto Único 2555 de 2010 (financial regulation), Circular Externa 004 de 2018 de la Superintendencia de Sociedades (Sarlaft and ultimate beneficial owner), Resolución UIAF 164 de 2017 (UBO identification and reporting)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Passport Office of Country of Origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Existence, Good Standing, and Legal Representation of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home country Companies Registry / Chamber of Commerce
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization if non-Hague state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney appointing the Colombian incorporation agent and representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in Country of Origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille and attached sworn Spanish translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Atomatic and manual screening of all shareholders, directors, legal representatives, and ultimate beneficial owners against the OFAC/SDN list, UN Consolidated Domestic and interpreted Colombian national security list (UIAF) prior to incorporation and at every transaction threshold under Sarlaft. Enhanced due diligence for PEPs and SENIOR SANCTIONS events applies from the pre-incorporation phase.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Único Empresarial – RUES (operated jointly with the Cámara de Comercio and Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company name must be formulated in Spanish or transliterated Latin script; custom or foreign words require an expulsion of meaning, and the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC) reserves the right to reject names likely to cause confusion with existing trademarks or official institutional marks.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected, the applicant may file a reconsideration petition before the same Cámara de Comercio within ten (10) business days. If such petition is denied, an administrative appeal may be brought before the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC) under the Código de Procedimiento Administrativo y de lo Contencioso Administrativo (CPACA). A new name reservation may also be initiated without prejudice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office addresses are generally accepted for S.A.S. incorporation as a registered office, provided they are a physical location where legal notices can be validly served. However, for ISIC 7020 (International Tax Structuring and Transfer Pricing Advisory), the Superintendencia de Sociedades expects a physical sub-office and a locally engaged administrative or professional representative to satisfy commercial substance and anti-avoidance parameters under the domestic tax CFC and substance-over-form doctrine.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 35% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection during the first fiscal year; expected to rise to 60% within three years due to the UBO registry verification and the SIC regulatory review of professional consultancy licenses.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Incorporation public deed and registration of the S.A.S. bylaws under Ley 1258 de 2008

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial tariff (Decreto 1644 de 1989) plus Registry registration tariff applied on the capital value

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and legalization/apostille of the foreign corporate documents and UBO identification bundle

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-document apostille fee and translator sworn fee under Colombian validation rules

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Accounting and local compliance upfront set-up for UBO report filing and Sarlaft implementation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory compliance filing fee and professional amount for Sarlaft manual preparation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Professional fees for local attorney, virtual office arrangement, and incorporation agency services

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for S.A.S. fast-track incorporation with cross-border shareholders

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Government registry fee in accordance with periodic SIC decree

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of the registered office address in the RUES and publication in the Chamber of Commerce bulletin

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008 (S.A.S. regime) arts. 1–48; Código de Comercio arts. 98, 110, 373–403; Decree 1074 of 2015 (Regulatory Decree of Commerce) arts. 1.1.1.1 et seq. and 13.2.2.1
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá); Superintendencia de Sociedades de Colombia (surveillance and corporate oversight)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución / Escritura Pública de Constitución (as applicable) registered in the Registro Mercantil of the local Cámara de Comercio
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital under Law 1258. At least one share must be subscribed, but payment may be deferred in the bylaws for up to two years. There is no escrow account requirement for capital contributions; paid-in funds may be deposited into an ordinary corporate bank account. Sectoral minimum capital rules may apply only if the company seeks regulated licenses (e.g., financial, outsourcing, or operational security services).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED BY THE FOUNDING SHAREHOLDERS OF SOCIEDAD: FIRST, that the subscription of one thousand (1,000) class A shares, subscribed and fully paid in cash, is hereby accepted and recorded in the share register. SECOND, that the registered office of the Company is established in Bogotá D.C., at Calle 100 No. 8A-50, Oficina 501, and the legal representative is instructed to file the corresponding registry entries before the Cámara de Comercio and to publish any notices required by law. THIRD, that [Full Name] is appointed as sole Manager and Legal Representative, and [Full Name] as Deputy Manager, with full authority to open bank accounts, execute contracts, and represent the Company in all public and private matters, in accordance with Law 1258 of 2008.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (via RUES online platform – rues.org.co)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the RUES portal or the local Chamber of Commerce website. Complete the homonym application form (Certificado de Homónimos) with at least three proposed company names. Pay the nominal search fee (approx. USD 2). Once the certificate confirms no identical existing registered name, the name is reserved for 30 calendar days.
required_dossiers: Shareholder identification (national ID or valid passport)
Proposed company names in order of preference
Power of attorney (if filing through an agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to preexisting similarity or protected trademark, submit an alternative name list. If no alternative exists, file a formal administrative petition (derecho de petición) before the Superintendencia de Sociedades requesting a name availability ruling.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of the Incorporation Document
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public for the company's domicile (notarization mandatory only for contributions of real estate or goods exceeding a specified value; otherwise private document)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the incorporation document and bylaws under Law 1258 of 2008. The document must include shareholders, capital subscription and payment terms, corporate object, domicile, management representation, and governance rules. If capital is paid in real estate, the incorporation must be executed as a public deed (Escritura Pública) before a Notary. For cash-only capital, execute as a private document (Documento Privado) signed by all shareholders.
required_dossiers: Draft bylaws / estatutos
Identification and contact details of each shareholder
Notarial deed (if public deed is required)
Capital contribution statement or bank deposit certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises objections to any clause, amend and restate the document before signature. Ensure all shareholder consents are formally ratified and notarized where required. Any defect in the document is cured before registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registration with the Chamber of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the signed incorporation document (private deed or public deed), the name reservation certificate, and payment of registration fees to the Registro Mercantil desk or through the RUES portal. Pay the regulatory registration fee and the certificate fee. Upon successful processing, the company obtains its Matrícula Mercantil and Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal, which constitutes the legal existence of the S.A.S.
required_dossiers: Incorporation document signed by shareholders
Name reservation certificate
Shareholder identification documents
Completed registration application forms (Registro Único Empresarial – RUES)
Proof of payment of registration fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Chamber of Commerce objects, correct the document and resubmit within five business days. If rejection persists, file a recurso de reposición under the Code of Administrative Procedure to preserve the application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal, complete the RUT (Registro Único Tributario) form electronically through the DIAN portal (dian.gov.co) or at a DIAN branch. Include the company CIIU code 7020, fiscal address, classification, and legal representative data. Obtain the NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria). Request an electronic invoicing resolution (Resolución de Facturación Electrónica) if the applicable turnover threshold is met or if the company opts for e-invoicing voluntarily.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
Legal representative's national ID or passport
RUT registration form completed online
Proof of registered office address (lease or utility bill)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DIAN issues a query or rejects the RUT due to missing information, correct the form online. If the tax classification is contested, file a derecho de petición with DIAN explaining the business activity and requested tariff classification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Corporate Bank Account and Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank selected by shareholders (e.g., Bancolombia, BBVA, Banco de Bogotá)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a business checking account in the company's name at a full-service commercial bank. Present the corporate formation documents, NIT/RUT, and the legal representative's identification to the corporate banking desk. Implement the paid-in capital deposit if set out in the bylaws, using wire transfer or cash payment. Preserve the deposit slip as proof for the Superintendencia de Sociedades and internal capital records.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
RUT / NIT
Bylaws / estatutos
Legal representative identification
Bank forms and beneficial ownership declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires enhanced due diligence or rejects the application, provide the requested beneficial ownership background and update the company record. If rejection continues, select another regulated financial institution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Operating License and Physical Safety Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Secretaría de Desarrollo Económico / Oficina de Planeación Municipal (zoning); Bomberos (fire safety); Administradora de Riesgos Laborales (ARL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the municipal land-use compatibility certificate (Certificado de Uso de Suelo) from the planning office for the office address. For physical premises, obtain the fire safety inspection certificate (Certificado de Bomberos). Register the Sistema de Gestión de Seguridad y Salud en el Trabajo (SG-SST) with an ARL authorized by the Ministry of Labor. Post the operating license in a visible location. For office-based consultancy, this set of clearances constitutes the statutory operational authorizations.
required_dossiers: Matrícula Mercantil and company certificate
Lease or property title of the office
Fire safety compliance plan and evacuation map
SG-SST implementation and ARL enrollment
Land-use / zoning certificate application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the land-use certificate is negative, file a zoning exception request with the Municipal Planning Council. For fire-safety defects, rectify the nonconformities and schedule a reinspection. For SG-SST issues, correct documentation with the ARL before commencing payroll.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (for commercial/industrial registration); Secretaría de Planeación Distrital o Municipal (for land-use and physical operation clearance); Superintendencia de Sociedades (for corporate governance oversight)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Matrícula Mercantil (Commercial Registration and Operating License) together with Certificado de Uso de Suelo, Certificado de Bomberos, and SG-SST enrollment – no separate sectoral industrial permit applies to office-based tax structuring and transfer pricing advisory (ISIC 7020).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Secretaría Distrital de Ambiente (or municipal environmental authority for the company's domicile); for any larger project, Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Category III: office-based consultancy does not trigger a mandatory Environmental Impact Assessment under Decree 1076 of 2015 (RUAA). A simple environmental registration or self-report is sufficient.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: N/A for process wastewater or VOC emissions. Must comply with municipal solid waste separation rules (Res. 2184/2019), e-waste management under Res. 1672/2013, and urban noise limits (Res. 0627/2006) of ≤55 dB in office areas.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate (Certificado de Bomberos) required for office premises with occupancy greater than 100 m²; structural verification from the local planning office for building occupancy; occupational health and safety clearance via an active SG-SST regime registered with an ARL; compliance with labor workplace conditions and emergency evacuation protocols.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN); official web portal: www.dian.gov.co; electronic services via the MUISCA platform (Sede Electrónica).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Foreign incorporators obtain the 'pre-RUT' provisional registration through the DIAN MUISCA site (www.muisca.dian.gov.co). Step 2: Execute the S.A.S. constitutive document (private instrument, no minimum capital; foreign ownership fully permitted) and record it with the Cámara de Comercio to obtain the matrícula mercantil (business registration). Step 3: Within thirty days of incorporation, file the definitive RUT with DIAN to be assigned the NIT and to assume fiscal responsibilities (income tax, VAT or IVA, source withholding, electronic invoicing; ICA municipal tax if applicable). Step 4: Register non-resident shareholders or a legal representative receiving Colombian-source payments in the RUT with character 'No Domiciliado' for the NIT; if a foreign parent receives dividends or fees, that NIT supports the remittance and transfer-pricing documentation. Step 5: Activate the electronic invoicing habilitation (software provider ID and digital certificate) and maintain the annual RUT update obligation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; the S.A.S. is a separate income-tax payer (no pass-through treatment) under Colombia's worldwide-taxation regime for resident entities; foreign non-resident shareholders are taxed on remittances/dividends only at source rates (0%-10% additional rate) with separate 'no domiciled' filing obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No general check-the-box election exists in Colombia. Specific elections available to the S.A.S. include: (i) SIMPLE (Simplified Taxation Regime) election, replacing income, VAT and industry-and-commerce tax with a presumptive single payment, limited to gross annual income not exceeding 100,000 UVT (tax year 2024 UVT = COP 47,065); and (ii) election to form a consolidated tax group ('grupo económico con consolidación') with related Colombian entities, subject to prior DIAN authorization. Hybrid mismatch treatment is mandatory (BEPS Action 2 transposed by Law 2010 of 2019); there is no elective hybrid-mismatch regime.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT / IVA (Impuesto al Valor Agregado; statutory title 'impuesto sobre las ventas')
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: VAT registration is compulsory from the first taxable sale, and a corporation (S.A.S.) cannot benefit from the 'no responsable de IVA' status, which is reserved for natural persons whose gross income is below 3,500 UVT (tax year 2024: approx. COP 164.7 million). Because consulting services under ISIC 7020 are taxable, the S.A.S. must register as a VAT responsible in the RUT immediately after incorporation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: MANDATORY REAL-TIME BILLING: Under DIAN Resolution 165/2023, the S.A.S. must obtain an electronic fiscal certificate (firma electrónica), be habilitated by DIAN to issue the Factura Electrónica de Venta (FEV), and transmit the standardized XML to DIAN's MUISCA web services (SOAP/API) so that the invoice is pre-validated before legal issuance. DIAN returns an acceptance/acknowledgment and the sealed invoice carries the unique electronic document code (CUDE); all post-issuance events (credit notes, transport events, export operations) are transmitted to RADIAN, DIAN's mandatory e-archive platform. No physical pre-printing or retrospective stamping is allowed; issuance to a foreign export client is filed under the special 'export operation' invoice event.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: zero-rating is conditioned on physical exit from Colombian customs territory under a definitive export declaration ('Declaración de Exportación' - DEX), sale to a non-resident, and collection of proceeds through the Colombian foreign-exchange market. Services: a consultancy service (ISIC 7020) qualifies as an 'export of services' only if it is rendered to a recipient not domiciled in Colombia, is used exclusively abroad, does not relate to assets or activities physically located in Colombia, and the price is paid by the non-resident in foreign currency remitted from abroad. The zero-rated nature must be reflected in the FEV invoice, and the resulting 'saldo a favor' (excess VAT credits) is recoverable against income tax or refundable at DIAN's discretion.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Goods/merchandise only: Customs Export Declaration (DEX - Declaración de Exportación) registered in DIAN/VUCE
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill or CMR transport document evidencing physical exit (goods), or delivery-and-acceptance protocol (services)
Inward Remittance Certificate / foreign-exchange settlement certificate (Certificado de Venta de Divisas or Certificado de Cambio) proving receipt from abroad
Services only: signed international service contract and, where available, the Certificado de Exportación de Servicios issued to the foreign client
VAT return (Form 300) and e-invoice export event in which the zero-rated operation and export exemption are reported
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN risk rules automatically match DEXs, e-invoice export events, transport documents and FX settlements; a false or unsupported export claim leads to (i) reversal of the zero-rating and collection of the 19% VAT, (ii) late payment interest under Art. 634 E.T., (iii) a 200% penalty on the difference for inexact returns when documentation is false (Art. 648 E.T.), and (iv) suspension or refusal of the refund claim; criminal exposure under Law 1762 of 2014 for smuggling ('contrabando') and fiscal fraud ('defraudación fiscal') includes imprisonment, fines and confiscation, with penalties aggravated when structured shells or sham service contracts are used.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Full name of the Central Bank or Foreign Exchange Administration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual renewal of mercantile registry (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the registered office jurisdiction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January to 31 March of the immediately following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal sanction of up to 17 UVT for each month or fraction in arrears; continued non-renewal causes the commercial registration to be cancelled and the company to be administratively struck off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual general meeting and deposit of financial statements (Estados Financieros)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements for the preceding fiscal year must be approved by shareholders within three months after 31 December and deposited with the Chamber by 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to deposit triggers Chamber refusal to certify compliance and a monetary fine of at least one minimum monthly wage, with recurring defaults used as grounds for administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Declaración de renta y complementarios)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: During the annual DIAN tax calendar for legal entities, fixed by NIT suffix and generally falling between June and October of the following fiscal year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of tax due per month or fraction thereof, capped at 100% of the tax, with a floor of 10 UVT; default interest applied from the original deadline.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual update of the Beneficial Owner Registry (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales, RUB)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within the window established by DIAN for that year, usually in the first quarter, with deadlines based on NIT suffix.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to update by the deadline generates a daily fine of 5 UVT per day of delay and may prevent the company from obtaining tax certificates or transacting with public entities.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Recording of annual board and shareholder meeting minutes (Actas de asamblea/junta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio, Register of Commercial Acts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Minutes of the annual shareholders' meeting approving the financial statements must be filed within 30 days of the meeting, which must be held no later than three months after fiscal year end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unregistered minutes cannot be asserted against third parties; failure to maintain registered corporate books may yield Chamber fines and impede subsequent execution of corporate resolutions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory auditor (revisor fiscal) is mandatory when gross assets exceed 5,000 SMMLV (approx. COP 7.0 billion) or gross income exceeds 3,000 SMMLV, or when required by shareholder agreement / supervisory authority; for other S.A.S. an internal audit may be optional but financial statements must be independently reviewed if the company is classified as Group 1 under IFRS.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as endorsed by Colombian law (Law 1314 of 2009): Full IFRS for Group 1 entities; IFRS for SMEs ('NIIF para las PYMES') for Group 2 entities, which is the ordinary standard for a consulting S.A.S.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each share transfer must be recorded in the register of members, and updated UBO details must be transmitted annually to DIAN through the RUB process. A share transfer without prior RUB update is deemed ineffective for corporate registration and triggers DIAN fines; the legal representative must ensure the UBO declaration is current at the deadline.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 – 2,400 per year for a virtual registered office and commercial agent in Bogotá
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,000 – 3,000 for initial IFRS SME financial statements with full audit; review-only may start at USD 600.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 35% under Article 240 E.T. for taxable years 2023 onward; S.A.S. entities in consultancy have no reduced statutory corporate rate.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No tax holidays for an ordinary S.A.S. under ISIC 7020. Effective rate is reduced through ordinary deductions: 100% of eligible operational costs, depreciation and amortization, and the qualifying 50% deduction for investments in research and technological development under Article 158-1 E.T., capped at 25% of net taxable income. No patent box or IP preferential regime applies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 210 - Declaración de Renta y Complementarios para personas jurídicas y asimiladas; mandatory electronic filing through DIAN MUISCA web services; supplemental XML attachments include certified financial statements and, where applicable, the transfer pricing return Form 120.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; fiscal year is generally the calendar year for a Colombian S.A.S. No consolidated filing; each legal entity files separately.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Under the annual DIAN Resolution, the Form 210 filing window opens in the ninth month after the fiscal year-end and closes in the tenth month; for FY ending 31 December 2024, deadlines are set by the last two digits of the NIT between 9 September 2025 and 9 October 2025. No general extension exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - NIT, razón social y tipo de contribuyente
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Colombian NIT, exact legal name of the S.A.S., address, CIIU code 7020, and taxpayer classification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Colombian entity must file using its own NIT. Non-resident shareholders do not file this return, but their NITs and residence jurisdictions are disclosed in the shareholder annex.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue from tax structuring and transfer pricing advisory services, including fees invoiced to foreign clients, converted to COP using the DIAN exchange rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Export services rendered from Colombia constitute Colombian-source income. Foreign client location does not exclude the income; treaty business-profit protection only applies if no permanent establishment exists in Colombia.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Contractual returns, rebates and discounts supported by credit notes in accordance with invoicing rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No non-resident-specific exemption; reductions require valid local electronic credit notes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Payroll, social contributions, software, rent, contractor fees, TP-consistent related-party charges, depreciation, amortization and other expenses causally related to taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Fees paid to foreign related parties are deductible only if supported by a functional analysis, arm's length pricing, and proof of 15% withholding tax if the payment is Colombian-source.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable ordinary income after allowable exemptions, NOL carryforward and prior-year compensation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders cannot offset Colombian taxable income with their foreign losses; NOL carryforward is computed solely at S.A.S. level.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits against CIT: foreign tax credit, income tax withheld at source by Colombian clients, and qualified R&D credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credit is available only to the Colombian taxpayer for foreign-source income; it cannot be claimed by the foreign parent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final CIT after credits before advance payments; calculated at 35% of taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This amount is unaffected by non-resident shareholder tax residency; distribution stage triggers separate dividend withholding.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty is 5% of final tax due for each month or fraction of month, up to 100%; if no tax is due the penalty is 15 UVT. Default interest accrues at the current DIAN rate. Failure to file after DIAN notice can raise the penalty to 20% of the assessment plus interest.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Pursuant to Article 245 E.T., dividends paid to non-resident shareholders out of profits already taxed at the corporate level are subject to a final 5% withholding tax. Dividends distributed from profits not taxed at the corporate level are subject to a 35% withholding tax. Treaty rates may reduce these amounts if the beneficial owner meets DTA conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The foreign shareholder must (1) obtain a current Certificate of Tax Residence from the treaty jurisdiction, notarized and apostilled where required; (2) submit the certificate to the Colombian withholding agent prior to payment; (3) complete and file DIAN Form 2970 or the applicable administrative application to activate treaty protection; (4) provide an ownership and beneficial-ownership declaration when the reduced treaty rate depends on a shareholding threshold; and (5) if excessive withholding occurred, file a refund claim with DIAN within the statutory two-year period supported by the TRC, dividend minutes and evidence of payment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest paid to non-residents is subject to a 15% domestic withholding tax, commonly reduced to 10% under DTAs. Royalties and technical-assistance fees paid to non-residents are subject to a 15% domestic withholding tax on Colombian-source income; treaty rates are typically 10% or 15% and require substance and beneficial ownership. Pure foreign-to-foreign services not exploited in Colombia are not Colombian-source.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File and Form 120 are mandatory for FY2024 when prior-year gross income is at least COP 4,706,500,000 (100,000 UVT) or gross assets are at least COP 7,059,750,000 (150,000 UVT), with reportable related-party transactions. Master File is required for members of multinational groups that meet the Colombian CbC threshold, aligned to the OECD EUR 750 million consolidated revenue threshold. Contemporaneous TP documentation remains advisable for all cross-border consultancy arrangements below these thresholds.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia does not operate an Emirates-style Economic Substance Regulations regime. However, DIAN applies general anti-avoidance rules, form-over-substance doctrine, beneficial ownership requirements, DTA limitation-on-benefits clauses, and the substantive permanent establishment tests. A Colombian S.A.S. must demonstrate real business purpose, local management, payroll, office or infrastructure and substantive execution of advisory functions; otherwise treaty benefits may be denied and the entity may be disregarded.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of Colombian-source advisory fees, use of undisclosed offshore collection accounts, fictitious deductions, or issuance of invoices to shell intermediaries with no operational substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties under Article 648 E.T. plus criminal liability under Article 434 A of the Colombian Criminal Code: imprisonment of 48 to 108 months, fines of up to 200% of the evaded tax, and mandatory publication of the sanction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and shareholders may be personally liable under Law 1258/2008 for the S.A.S. where the entity is used as a façade. Civil restitution, asset attachment, exit/travel restrictions imposed by the criminal process, disqualification from corporate management and imprisonment are available.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file Form 120 or the Local File despite exceeding statutory thresholds; deliberate use of non-arm's length margins in cross-border management fees; lack of functional analysis or contemporaneous documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN makes transfer pricing adjustments increasing taxable income; the underpayment carries a 20% inaccuracy penalty plus default interest. Failure to file the TP return triggers article 651 E.T. penalties computed on gross income or assets, capped by UVT limits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative and revisor fiscal who certifies false TP information may face civil liability for the additional tax, professional sanctions, disqualification, and criminal prosecution for false documentation.
